newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil appoints senator to oversee pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil appoints senator to oversee pension reform.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Thursday took a first step toward reviving pension reform legislation when a senator was appointed to take charge of the bill in the upper house, a presidential spokesman said.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso also hopes a reform of the civil service would be put to a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies either during the current special session of Congress, which ends February 6, or shortly after, Sergio Amaral said.

Sen. Benedito Veras, a member of Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party, was named to oversee the pension reform bill which was approved in July in the lower house in a watered-down form. Since then, the legislation has awaited a Senate rewrite.

The government wants to take advantage of political momentum generated on Tuesday by the first approval in the Chamber of Deputies of a bill allowing Cardoso's re-election. Progress on the government's reforms had stalled while the house considered the re-election bill.
The pension reform would end an array of perks for public sector workers and make all Brazilians contribute to their pension plans.
Under the current system, the amount of time workers have serve in their jobs, and not the amount of contributions they have made, determines who is entitled a state pension.
Government officials say the reform is needed to prevent Brazil's social security system from going further into deficit.

The civil service reform is considered vital to attempts to rein in public spending because it would allow states and municipal governments to dismiss workers whose jobs are currently safe and bring order to pubic finances.

Earlier, Cardoso told reporters he wanted Congress to press on with the government's reforms but recognized internal elections, to choose the new presidents of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, would have to come first.
